_why: Seed boxes for the library fights, each one confirmed by looking at the
frame rather than picked by a rule. Every automatic rule tried here has
chosen at least one non-fighter: 'the two largest non-referee detections
on frame 0' picks a seated coach as fighter B on two of the three fights,
and the analysis then spends the bout holding a chair. That is not a
hypothetical - it produced a whole afternoon of fighter-B measurements
that were really measurements of furniture, and coverage went UP when the
tracking got worse, because a man in a chair is easy to keep covered.
The product itself never does this: the coach draws both boxes by hand.
The rule only exists in measurement harnesses, which is exactly where it
does the most damage, because nobody is looking at the frames.
So: measure from these, or from boxes you have looked at. Never from a
rule. See tools/measure_identity.py, which reads this file and renders a
sheet of what it actually tracked so the next person can check too.
_convention: fighter_a is the blue-kit fighter in all three, so numbers can be read across fights.

5736.note: Broadcast single mat. A is the blue fighter, B the red one. Verified at frame 700, where the detector separates both fighters and the seated coaches at x 357-397. On frame 0 the second-largest detection is one of those coaches, which is what the old rule picked.
5736.kit: blue vs red - the only fight in the library that carries a real corner colour

b883.note: Multi-mat hall, 13-18 people in shot, several bouts at once - so 'which two' is a real question and the answer is the pair on the near mat. Verified at frame 4400 mid-exchange, A kicking, B punching. Earlier frames merge B with the white-shirted referee.
b883.kit: blue vs black - no corner colour at all, which is the normal case

1mp4.note: A is the blue fighter centre-frame, B the dark-kit opponent to their left. Frame 0 shows only one person, so this fight cannot be seeded at the start at all. The seated coach at x 368-411 is what the old rule picked as B.
